svg.title: Console result page: QR codes
svg.desc: A mockup of a 640 x 480 console screen with no data: a header, a white panel with six placeholder QR patterns in two rows of three and a text index beside each row, and lines for the version, error correction, byte counts and a CRC32 over all payloads. Numbered notes on the right explain each part and what is still open.
svg.text: A console result page: QR codes
MOCKUP, NO DATA. A layout for a page of QR codes. The codes are placeholder patterns, not readable codes; #### are placeholders.
Status: MEASURED our console · FACT a manual or our code · ESTIMATE our arithmetic or model · OPEN not known
The screen at 1:1, 640 x 480; one character of the console font is 12 x 24 px.
RAY1 P10/24 QR 1/2 6 CODES
Q1 ##B
Q2 ##B
Q3 ##B
Q4 ##B
Q5 ##B
Q6 ##B
V3-M 6 X ##B ##### B IN ALL
CRC32 ######## ALL 6 IN ORDER
MEAS
EST
TEXT P09
action-safe, 32 / 24 px in (90 %)
title-safe, 64 / 48 px in (80 %)
REPORTED: the usual SD overscan margins; every word and digit sits inside title-safe.
What each part is for
Header: image, page, which part of the set (QR 1/2) and
how many codes are on the screen.
Codes dark on white, each with a 4-module quiet zone
(16 px here; neighbours share it). Drawn as version 3,
29 x 29 modules at 4 px a module, 6 a page.
Index in plain text: which code holds which bytes, so a
photo that misses one shows it.
Version, error correction, bytes each and in all. V3-M
holds 42 bytes, V5-M 84 [REPORTED: the standard's table,
not checked here]: 6 x 42 = 252 bytes a page.
CRC32 over every payload in order: the reader checks the
set is whole. Legend slots; the text page it repeats.
Rules for every page
· Placeholder patterns: no code here can be scanned.
· Module size and version from a phone test on the real TV
and cable [OPEN]; 4 px modules may blur on composite
[ESTIMATE].
· Payload: the test's RESULT lines as plain text, so any
phone app shows them as is; field format not set [OPEN].
· Encoder: our own C (Reed-Solomon over GF(256)) or a
library whose licence allows it, credited; none chosen [OPEN].
· An extra page, not a replacement: the text page stays,
so a run with no phone app still has the numbers.
